comparator.sourceNotes: This 180 EC example comprises 60 EC of foundation courses, 65 EC of restricted electives, 30 EC of free electives and a 25 EC graduation phase.

core: Environmental natural sciences linking Earth, water, soils, ecosystems and human activity
Environmental problem analysis using mathematics, data, experiments and research methods
Climate, energy, circular-resource and sustainability transitions
adjacent: Biodiversity, pollution, ecosystem resilience and food-environment relations
Environmental policy, decision-making and science-practice connections
Renewable energy, circular systems and environmental economics
Environmental data, GIS, modelling, hypotheses and scientific communication
questions: How do coupled Earth and ecological systems respond to human pressures?
How can evidence be used to analyse and solve environmental problems?
Which technological, economic and governance choices enable sustainable transitions?

alternatives.label: Environmental Systems and Applied Research
alternatives.labelReason: Study Earth systems, ecosystems, soils and water through field observation, data and environmental chemistry. Apply this understanding to sustainable farming, climate and resource use.
alternatives.concept: Study Earth systems, ecosystems, soils and water through field observation, data and environmental chemistry. Apply this understanding to sustainable farming, climate and resource use.
progression: The sustainability gateways support later environmental study. Introductory biodiversity precedes advanced ecosystem study. Data preparation and mathematics precede later quantitative analysis.

alternatives.label: Climate, Energy and Circular Systems
alternatives.labelReason: Study climate change and renewable energy, then analyze energy-system design, material recovery and product life cycles. Use economics and communication to examine how communities respond to environmental change.
alternatives.concept: Study climate change and renewable energy, then analyze energy-system design, material recovery and product life cycles. Use economics and communication to examine how communities respond to environmental change.
progression: The sustainability gateways precede energy study and design. Economics and research methods precede policy, behavioral economics and econometrics.
alternatives.distinctness: Study climate change and renewable energy, then analyze energy-system design, material recovery and product life cycles. Use economics and communication to examine how communities respond to environmental change. Each plan has 10 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1.

alternatives.label: Environmental Policy and Public Participation
alternatives.labelReason: Study how institutions and communities respond to environmental problems. Combine policy analysis, economics and social research with environmental science, public communication and environmental justice.
alternatives.concept: Study how institutions and communities respond to environmental problems. Combine policy analysis, economics and social research with environmental science, public communication and environmental justice.
progression: Environmental and social foundations precede environmental observation, policy analysis and civil society. Introductory data work precedes econometrics.
alternatives.distinctness: Study how institutions and communities respond to environmental problems. Combine policy analysis, economics and social research with environmental science, public communication and environmental justice. Each plan has 14 courses absent from the other when compared with option 1. Each plan has 13 courses absent from the other when compared with option 2.

notes.text: The UCR options combine environmental science with applied research, energy and materials, or public policy. Open Universiteit requires separate foundation courses in chemistry, physics and physiology, an integrated practicum and a supervised graduation project.

selection.assessment: The closest plan combines physical environmental processes, ecology, pollution and agricultural systems with applied research. It covers food production and environmental impacts, with specialist food safety and toxicology remaining gaps. The energy plan concentrates on technology, materials and economics. The policy plan concentrates on institutions, public decisions and participation. All three maintain environmental science foundations.
